title: The 2017-2025 Kuroshio large meander raised Kii-Tokai-Izu coastal sea level by about 9 cm, as five earlier meanders predict, and the rise reversed after April 2025 (JMA tide gauges, 1966-2026)
abstract: Question: did the longest Kuroshio large meander (LM) since 1965 (August 2017 to April 2025) change coastal sea level, high-water days and coastal SST south of Japan by the amounts that the five earlier LMs (1975-2005) predict, and did the changes reverse after the LM ended? Approach: hourly JMA tide-gauge data (26 gauges, to September 2026) and NOAA OISST v2.1. For each gauge and event, a regression with a local linear trend and season gave the LM effect on monthly level relative to two upstream gauges (Aburatsu, Tosa-Shimizu). The mean of the earlier events is the out-of-sample prediction for 2017-2025. Results: at eight gauges from Uragami to Izu-Oshima the 2017-2025 effect was 7.1-10.9 cm (regional index 9.3 cm, SE 1.2; prediction 8.4 cm). Across 13 Pacific gauges, observed and predicted effects agreed (r = 0.98, slope 1.11, RMSE 1.0 cm). West of Cape Shionomisaki the effect was near zero. After the end, the regional level fell by 9.9 cm in 12 months (placebo p = 0.002); earlier end steps were -5.4 to -14.4 cm. The post-end level was 2.6 cm below 2014-2017, but this is within normal variation after a path-index fit. Days above the local 1%-of-days high-water level were 2.7-5.1 times more frequent during the LM at the eight gauges, as the mean shift alone predicts, and fell to 0.2-0.8% after the end. Coastal SST off Tokai rose 0.9-1.7 C in 2017-2025, more than in earlier events, but the first 13-20 months gave 0.36-0.60 C, the same as earlier events; the SST effect grew for three years while sea level responded in the first year. Limitations: six events only; the reference gauges and large-scale signals can contribute 1-2 cm (raw-level effect 6.7 cm); vertical land motion is only removed as a linear trend; 17 months of post-end data; OISST coastal resolution changed with time. Code, derived monthly and daily levels, aggregate results, figures and raw-file hashes are included; raw JMA and OISST files are retrieved by script.
